subject: biology
title: Sexually transmitted infections
key_idea: A sexually transmitted infection (STI) is passed on by sexual contact. Chlamydia and gonorrhoea are caused by bacteria and HIV by a virus. Spread is reduced by avoiding sexual contact, using a condom, not sharing needles, screening and treatment.

sections.heading: Common STIs and how they spread

blocks.text: STIs are communicable diseases passed on by sexual contact. This section compares chlamydia, gonorrhoea and HIV.

rows: Thick yellow or green discharge and pain on urinating. Many strains are resistant to penicillin.
Sexual contact, or exchange of body fluids
Destroys white blood cells. Can lead to AIDS.

items: HIV first causes a flu-like illness. It attacks the immune cells, and late-stage HIV infection is called AIDS.
In AIDS the immune system is so badly damaged that it cannot deal with other infections or cancers.
Drug users who share needles can pass on HIV in blood.
HIV can also pass in blood transfusions, and from a mother to the foetus in the uterus.
HIV is diagnosed by blood tests. Blood samples must be handled safely: wear gloves or goggles, cover cuts, clean up spills, store samples in sealed containers and dispose of them safely.
Chlamydia and gonorrhoea are caused by bacteria. HIV is caused by a virus.
All three spread by sexual contact. HIV also spreads in body fluids such as blood.
An STI is communicable because it is passed from person to person.

blocks.text: Prevention works by stopping the pathogen passing between people, or by treating infected people.

items: Avoid sexual contact.
Use a barrier method of contraception, such as a condom.
Do not share needles.
Screen people for an infection, and screen blood used for transfusions.
Treat bacterial STIs with antibiotics, and HIV with antiretroviral drugs.
Better education about how to prevent the spread of HIV can reduce new cases.
Condoms and avoiding sexual contact stop the pathogen passing on.
Antibiotics treat bacterial STIs. Antiretroviral drugs control HIV.
Not sharing needles and screening blood stop HIV spreading in blood.

blocks.text: Exam questions give the number of people diagnosed per 1000 of the population. Multiply by the population, then divide by 1000.

diagram.alt: A calculation practice: find the number of people diagnosed with an infection from a rate per 1000 and a population.
diagram.question: In one year, {rate} people per 1000 of the population were diagnosed with chlamydia. The population was {pop} people. Calculate the number of people diagnosed.

items: A rate per 1000 lets countries or years of different size be compared.
Divide the population by 1000, then multiply by the rate.

checks.q: Give two ways to prevent the spread of HIV.
checks.a: Any two from: avoid sexual intercourse, use a condom, do not share needles, use antiretroviral drugs, screen blood used for transfusions.

checks.q: State why chlamydia can be described as a communicable disease.
checks.a: It is passed (spread) from person to person, or it is caused by bacteria (a pathogen).

checks.q: Give one other way, apart from antibiotics, to control the spread of gonorrhoea.
checks.a: Use a condom (a barrier method of contraception), or avoid sexual intercourse.

worked_example.question: Give two ways to prevent the spread of HIV.
worked_example.tip: Any two score one mark each. If no other marks are awarded, "do not exchange body fluids" gets one mark.

worked_example.question: Chlamydia is a sexually transmitted infection (STI). Give one way the transmission of chlamydia can be prevented.
answer_points: Use a condom or femidom (a barrier form of contraception is accepted).
Treat the infection or give antibiotics.
worked_example.tip: Any one of these scores the mark. Protection and contraception unqualified are ignored.

worked_example.question: Which statement is correct about HIV/AIDS? A: AIDS is a virus that weakens the immune system. B: HIV and AIDS are alternative names for the same disease. C: HIV is a pathogen and AIDS is a set of infections. D: HIV is a virus that produces toxins which kill an infected person.
answer_points: C: HIV is a pathogen and AIDS is a set of infections.
worked_example.tip: HIV is the virus. AIDS is the set of infections that follows when the immune system is badly damaged.

worked_example.question: Describe how the spread of STIs, such as chlamydia, can be controlled.
answer_points: Education about the risks, how STIs are transmitted and how to prevent them.
worked_example.tip: Any four score one mark each.

blocks.text: More detail on HIV and STIs.

items: HIV can pass from a mother to her infant during pregnancy or in breast milk.
The risk is reduced if the mother takes HIV medication, the baby is delivered by caesarean section and the mother does not breastfeed.
Contact tracing finds the sexual partners of an infected person, so they can be tested and treated.
Vaccination is available against some STIs.
